details: is a speech synthesis program released in 1982 for the Magnavox Odyssey². It was designed by Robert Cheezum for North American Philips and released exclusively in North America as a launch title for the Odyssey²'s voice synthesis module, "The Voice of Odyssey²". Users can enter a short phrase which the voice module will attempt to read. Critics thought it was too simple to hold anyone's attention for long but were entertained by getting the voice module to say a wide variety of things.

explainer.lead: Type & Tell! is a speech synthesis program released in 1982 for the Magnavox Odyssey². It matters as an early consumer example of user-entered text being spoken aloud.

tiers.eli5: You type a short phrase into a game console and a voice module tries to say it out loud.
tiers.practitioner: It is a historical reference point for text-to-speech on consumer hardware rather than a current engineering tool. A pitfall in assessing it is expecting more than reading short typed phrases.
tiers.paperLevel: It was designed by Robert Cheezum for North American Philips and released exclusively in North America as a launch title for the Voice of Odyssey² module; users enter a short phrase the module attempts to read. Limit: it handled only short phrases.

explainer.example: A user types a short phrase on the Odyssey² and the voice module attempts to pronounce it.
